title: So long, folks!
author: Charming_You_25
selftext:
I just wanted to make the most amazing game idea I’ve ever had— a mmo, ai dnd / dungeon crawler Carl inspired, crafting system inspired by an inversion if infinite craft... people said “dont make a multiplayer game for your first game” and “don’t write your own engine”. I didnt listen. I wrote my own engine, 800,000 lines of code later… it’s still not something id be proud to release and is so mindbogglingly complex and a time suck im putting it down for the forseeable future to explore other ideas. I’m still learning game design and my idea is too good for me to just release slop that requires massive buy in from lots of people. 

But that’s not why I’m turning from game design being my main focus.. you see, I had a bug. A really, really tricky bug that comes from LLMs multidimensional space in their weights. Yesterday, I finally solved it. And in doing so, accidentally created  a generator that can be used to make novel prompt injections that has worked everywhere I tried them.

I’m still verifying everything, and will release a couple new types of benchmarks in the next week, and do whatever disclosures my agent suggests. I feel like I should write a paper, but, I’m not an academic. 

If you take this as a big nothing i won’t blame you. It’s just the way I operate, going off what seems most probable, sometimes with little to back it up. I’m usually right, and my intuition is telling me I cracked something novel.

I just wanted to make a fucking game and instead found a loaded gun.

Even if this doesn’t pan out: writing the story to my game and writing a new TOS where I traded potential money for my players privacy has made me realize I care deeply about how AI is going to break for humanity. So I’m going to start seeking positions in model alignment. RIP my game design career. Dead before its birth.

I labeled this a discussion so I’ll end with a question: what interesting things have you learned incidentally while making a game?

replies.author: Charming_You_25
replies.body:
Yes. I get yall are taking the piss but I’m concerned if I’m specific it could be legitimately dangerous.

I guess I made the post because I’m in awe how at how weird ai game dev is. You never know what’s going to come out of it. It’s huge and eats everything. Like your mom.

comments.author: HelpfulCabinet1560
comments.body: share it in DM or no balls

comments.author: Alone_Job3924
comments.body: That's quite a journey! It's wild how a project can lead you somewhere completely unexpected. I think it's great that you're taking the potential security risks seriously instead of rushing to release something. Sometimes the biggest discoveries happen when we're just trying to solve a problem. Even if your game is on hold, all that work wasn't wasted.

replies.author: Charming_You_25
replies.body: Thank you. It’s definitely not wasted. I have a huge library now I can pull from, and have done more spikes than I can count so I have a good idea what ai can and can’t do and the edge of what’s possible (and what needs breakthroughs before it becomes possible). My one shots are getting way better using already thought through architecture and ui as a base. I’ll post some here soon.
